title: Published Week 10 injury snapshot is stale against the official page
finding: The repository publishes 254 injury rows and states 279 as the live count. The official page publishes 347 rows at 2026-11-16T01:17Z. That is 68 more than published and 93 more than the stated live count.
status: Unresolved. The cause is not established: the official page may have grown, the earlier transcription may have been partial, or both. Both numbers are published rather than reconciled.
what_would_clear_it: Re-capture on a schedule and diff row by row. Do not overwrite the old snapshot before the diff is recorded.

title: A player appears under a club he was traded away from six days earlier
finding: Daiyan Henley was traded from the Chargers to the Broncos on 11/10. The Week 10 injury report retrieved on 11/16 still lists him under the Chargers, with full participation and no game designation.
status: Flagged, not reconciled. Both pages are official. Which one is current for the purposes of a pre-kickoff model is a question for replay, not for a guess now.
what_would_clear_it: Join every availability row to the transactions log and surface the conflict, which is requirement R46.

title: Twelve of thirteen Week 11 stadiums come from a link parameter, not a venue field
finding: The stadium strings were read from the destinationAddress.location parameter of the Marriott link the schedule page renders under each fixture. That is published by nfl.com but it is a commercial-link parameter.
status: One of thirteen was confirmed against the game centre's own Game Info field and matched. The other twelve are labelled link-parameter-sourced and are not certified.
what_would_clear_it: Read the Game Info block for one fixture per club, which is suggestion S03.

title: Week 10 results are single-sourced
finding: All twelve final scores were read from the official by-week schedule page at one moment. They have not been cross-checked against a second official page, such as a game centre or a Game Book.
status: Published as single-sourced. No score has been inferred; the two games that had not kicked off are left blank.
what_would_clear_it: Cross-check against the game centre for each completed game before the scores enter a results feed.

title: Capture times come from the sandbox clock
finding: No external time service is reachable from the sandbox, so every retrieval time is the sandbox UTC clock read with date -u, and individual fetch times were not recorded separately.
status: Each capture records a window rather than a single instant, and the window is stated on the page.
what_would_clear_it: Record a timestamp per fetch from a trusted source once one is reachable, or record the HTTP Date header of the response.

title: Only one of six captures retains its raw bytes and hash
finding: CAP-01 (the injury report) is committed verbatim with a SHA-256. CAP-02 to CAP-06 were transcribed into structured records without retaining the raw markdown, so they cannot be re-hashed.
status: Stated per capture in the manifest. No claim of immutability is made for the five transcribed captures.
what_would_clear_it: Retain raw bytes for every future capture, which is requirement R30.

title: Two Week 10 games had not kicked off at capture time
finding: Steelers at Bengals (8:20 PM ET, 15 November) and Chargers at Ravens (8:15 PM ET, 16 November) had not started when the pages were read, at 2026-11-16T01:17Z UTC, which is 20:17 ET on 15 November.
status: Their score cells are blank on the official page and blank here. Their designations are pre-game designations, not outcomes.
what_would_clear_it: Re-read after kickoff if those games are to enter the results feed.

title: The deficiency matrix shows designations, not strings travelled
finding: No verified depth order exists for all 32 clubs, so the matrix cannot show a first-string receiver against a third-string corner. It shows game-status designations by position group instead.
status: Published as a placeholder with the limitation stated on the page. It is not the feature that requirement R45 asks for.
what_would_clear_it: Resolve the depth-order source for 32 of 32 clubs first, which is requirement R52 and suggestion S10.

title: Four clubs have no injury rows at all, and that is not health
finding: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay were on bye in Week 10, so the official report publishes no rows for them.
status: Shown explicitly as on bye rather than as zero injuries. The per-team table carries 28 of 32 clubs for this reason.
what_would_clear_it: Carry the bye flag into every availability view, so an empty row is never read as a clean bill of health.

title: The reserve list covers one month
finding: Twenty-five reserve-list moves were captured for November 2026. Players placed on reserve in earlier months do not appear, so absence from this list is not evidence of availability either.
status: Stated on the page with the capture window.
what_would_clear_it: Backfill the season, which is suggestion S13.

title: Two implementations of the same origination brief exist
finding: A market board on the main dashboard and the origination desk implement the same eight requirements on different inputs, so they can publish different model lines for the same game.
status: Inherited from earlier sessions as flag OD-16 and question Q-21. Recorded here because a reviewer reading this desk will hit it. Not resolved by this session.
what_would_clear_it: An owner decision, which is suggestion S04 and owner decision O01.

title: The Texans depth chart is published as an image
finding: Houston publishes its depth chart in a form that does not parse to text. No authorized structured alternative was obtained.
status: Not transcribed. No depth rows are published for Houston from this session.
what_would_clear_it: An authorized structured source, or a recorded absence for the club in the P07 sweep.

title: NFL.com Terms section 1.3 prohibits the systematic capture this desk was asked to specify
finding: Section 1.3 of the NFL.com Terms of Service, updated 16 May 2024 and read on 2026-11-16, states: "Systematic retrieval of data or other content from the Services, whether to create or compile, directly or indirectly, a collection, compilation, database, or directory, is prohibited absent our express prior written consent." That blocks automated multi-day snapshots (R29, R30), a scheduled Wednesday-to-kickoff series (R54, R55), a past-season archive (R66), and any per-club sweep (R13, R23, R32, R43, R52). It also applies to work already committed: this session made six fetches and committed one verbatim 49,582-byte capture plus structured transcriptions.
status: Blocked by permission, not by work. Five requirements were re-marked as blocked and four suggestions were re-marked as blocked on permission. An earlier session reached the same conclusion independently and recorded it as DEC-01; this session re-read the terms page rather than relying on that record. No further capture has been run since.
what_would_clear_it: An owner decision with one of three outcomes: obtain express written consent, re-scope the affected requirements to what the terms permit, or remove the committed capture. Recorded as owner decision O05.

title: Three per-requirement readiness registers now exist
finding: readiness/ publishes 82 requirement rows, verification/ publishes 74, and this desk publishes 73. Three different counts for the same brief. An earlier session recorded the two-register version as VF-11; this session adds a third.
status: Flagged, not adjudicated. This session did not read either other register line by line, so it makes no claim about which is better. Cross-linked from the landing page.
what_would_clear_it: One register designated canonical. Recorded as owner decision O06.
